prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S196: Substation Field Crew verifies equipment indications locally when remote status is uncertain and reports discrepancies through established operating channels.
S197: Maintenance windows are planned around feeder loading, switching constraints, and the availability of qualified personnel.
S198: The Substation Supervisor coordinates work timing with the Switching Desk Coordinator and confirms that operating responsibilities are understood.
S199: The Control Room Operator reviews the equipment affected by each work package and identifies any required operating restrictions.
S200: The Switching Desk Coordinator confirms switching prerequisites before field work begins and keeps the approved switching sequence current.
S201: Substation Field Crew performs work only after required clearances, isolation, and grounding have been confirmed through established procedures.
S202: Work boundaries are verified locally before personnel approach exposed conductors or operate equipment under maintenance.
S203: The Protection Relay Engineer reviews test scope, approved settings, and restoration criteria before protection testing starts.
S204: Testing is performed with approved procedures, calibrated instruments, and a defined means of stopping the test if unexpected indications occur.
S205: The Engineering Workstation is used for authorized configuration review, and changes are applied only through station change control.
S206: The Maintenance Remote Terminal uses the review receipt to support controlled maintenance review.
S207: The Bay Automation Controller uses the load test record to support maintenance review.
S208: The Station Supervisory Control System receives the Protocol Retry Summary for operational review.
S209: Cinder verifies that field work remains within the approved work boundary and reports any unsafe condition through established channels.
S210: Orchard retains event information needed to review testing and restoration activity.
S211: Feeder Protection Relay testing is coordinated so that protection coverage is not unintentionally removed from an energized feeder.
S212: A protection function placed out of service is tracked by the responsible operator until it is restored and verified.
S213: The Breaker Control Unit is tested using controlled commands that cannot bypass local interlocks or approved operating authority.
S214: Remote commands are inhibited when equipment status is uncertain or when required permissives are unavailable.
S215: If communications are degraded, the Control Room Operator treats remote indications as unavailable until their reliability is established.
S216: Substation Field Crew verifies equipment indications locally when remote status is uncertain and reports discrepancies through established operating channels.
S217: Manual operation is permitted only under approved procedures and with the required local checks and communication with the Control Room Operator.
S218: A suspected controller or relay fault is assessed before any restart, bypass, or replacement is attempted.
S219: Restoration includes confirming normal indications, protection availability, communications status, and the removal of temporary test connections.
S220: The Substation Supervisor confirms that required records are complete and that operating restrictions are formally cleared before returning equipment to normal service.
S221: Operational assurance at Alder Creek depends on clear authority, verified equipment state, and records that support later review.
S222: The Control Room Operator remains responsible for deciding whether an automation request is appropriate for current operating conditions.
S223: The Bay Automation Controller shall execute only commands permitted by its approved logic and configured interlocks.
S224: The Feeder Protection Relay shall retain its protective function independently of supervisory communications.
S225: The Protection Relay Engineer reviews protection behavior after material changes and records any unresolved concerns for operational follow-up.
S226: The Station Supervisory Control System presents control indications and command results for operator assessment.
S227: The Sequence Event Archive retains time-ordered records needed to reconstruct significant control and protection events.
S228: The Engineering Workstation shall be used for authorized configuration work under established change control.
S229: The Satellite Time Receiver supports consistent event timing, and time-quality concerns shall be investigated before records are relied upon for sequence analysis.
S230: The Station Gateway shall maintain the defined boundary between station automation and external communications.
S231: The Station DC System shall be confirmed available before switching that depends on station control power.
S232: The Breaker Control Unit shall reject commands that do not satisfy its configured permissive conditions.
S233: Substation Field Crew uses the Isolation Boundary Card to verify the approved work boundary before entering the controlled area.
S234: Substation Field Crew reports unexpected equipment conditions promptly and pauses work when the approved boundary is uncertain.
S235: Switching Desk Coordinator receives the Clearance Handoff Memo and confirms that its clearance status agrees with the active switching record.
S236: Keystone shall confirm that switching authority, equipment state, and communication limits are understood before coordinating any automation-enabled action.
S237: The Substation Supervisor verifies that unresolved risks have an assigned owner and an agreed disposition before normal service is resumed.
S238: The Control Room Operator confirms indications locally when remote status is incomplete, inconsistent, or delayed.
S239: The Protection Relay Engineer assesses unexplained trips and abnormal protection indications before protection is returned to service.
S240: The Maintenance Remote Terminal shall use controlled access, and each maintenance session shall be attributable to an authorized user.
S241: The North Bay Controller shall be checked for expected local behavior after approved configuration work.
